newsitem.title: UK: Eurofighter partners see process still on track.
newsitem.headline: Eurofighter partners see process still on track.

text.p: Representatives of the four nations involved in the Eurofighter programme on Thursday reaffirmed their commitment to moving to production of the combat aircraft early next year, but gave no new details on timing.

In a joint statement issued after a meeting here, officials said that after the final national decisions on approval, awaited in the first quarter of next year, contracts would be concluded "to enable work to get under way promptly".
The key oustanding decision on Eurofighter is to be made in Germany early next year when the parliament is due to vote.
German representative state secretary Gunnar Simon assured the meeting Germany would complete its approval processes in early 1997, Britain's Press Association news agency reported.

The Partners in the Eurofighter consortium -- British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace, Alenia of Italy and Spain's Casa -- hoped their governments would have a memorandum of understanding on the project by the end of 1997.
In today's statement, the officials also noted the importance "of coordinated action to achieve price reductions during contractual negotiations".
"The success of the flight test programme provides increasing confidence that the very demanding specification of the Eurofighter will be met," they added.
Germany hopes to order 140 Eurofighters as fighters and another 40 as attack aircraft. Britain wants 232 planes from the project, Italy is slated to take 140 and Spain 87.
